subject: MAP draft: Acme POC — env dependencies & next steps
summary: Post-call MAP follow-up capturing POC environment dependencies (VPC peering, IP allowlists, SSO/SAML, secrets/KMS), milestone owners, and target close date. Waiting on Cloud Ops to confirm IP ranges and peering window; procurement looped for contract timeline.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Subject: MAP draft: Acme POC — env dependencies & next steps

Hi Alex — great call today, thanks again for taking the time. Per our discussion I'm attaching a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for the POC with Acme. High level summary and next steps below. Please review and let me know any changes to responsibilities or timelines.

Objective: 2-week POC validating Redwood inference in Acme's VPC (private deployment) with 5k daily inference volume target.

Key MAP milestone (POC environment setup) — blockers & owners:
- VPC peering (owner: Cloud Ops / Acme) — requirement: route to Redwood VPCs; target peering window: week of Jan 26
- IP allowlist (owner: Acme Cloud Ops) — Redwood egress IPs required for initial pull (see attached network diagram)
- SSO / SAML (owner: Acme ID team; Redwood to support) — configure SAML metadata and test users for SSO by Jan 25
- Secrets / KMS (owner: Acme Security) — KMS key access & secrets rotation policy; Redwood requires a service principal with decrypt access by Jan 25

Dependencies: network peering + IP allowlist must be completed before we run the first end-to-end inference test. SSO and KMS can be staged but should be ready before canary UAT.

Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan_Acme_v1.docx (MAP draft) and acme-network-diagram.png

Requested next steps:
1) Can Cloud Ops confirm available peering windows next week (Jan 26–30)?
2) Alex — can you confirm the primary contact for SAML and KMS?
3) I'll update the MAP with any changes and circulate a final copy by Wed (Jan 20).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP draft: Acme POC — env dependencies & next steps

Thanks Marissa — quick technical notes from my side:

- VPC peering: we'll need 2-way routing for the peered subnets and allow TCP 443/8443 (control plane + metrics) between Redwood management subnets and Acme POC subnets. I'll send the exact CIDR ranges in a separate email once Cloud Ops confirms peering window.
- IP allowlists: for the initial POC we expect outbound callbacks from the POC host to Redwood at these egress IPs: 34.82.112.45, 34.82.112.46 (subject to final infra config). Please add to Acme allowlist.
- SSO/SAML: we support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows. For the POC, IdP-initiated is fine — we only need SAML metadata and 2 test accounts.
- Secrets/KMS: we can support either AWS KMS or HashiCorp Vault. If Acme prefers KMS, we request a grant for the Redwood service principal to decrypt the POC secrets.

I'll attach a short checklist (technical) in the MAP doc. If Cloud Ops wants to run through the peering steps on a quick call I can join — available Tue/Thu morning PST.

—
Nikhil Sharma
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.com

- IP allowlist: confirmed — we can add the two egress IPs you listed to our firewall rules; please provide a companion FQDN if available.

- KMS/Secrets: we will provision a dedicated KMS key for the POC and create a role with decrypt permission for the Redwood service principal. We need the principal ARN and a short runbook for key rotation expectations.
